_schema.description: Single source of truth for the literature matrix and bibliography. Edit this file, then run: python research/tools/build_literature.py

verified_values.web-2026-10-01: Bibliographic details checked against a web source (arXiv/publisher/proceedings page) on 2026-10-01. Claims summarised from abstract or fetched page, NOT full-text reading unless noted.
verified_values.memory-verify: Classic/well-known reference entered from memory. Details believed correct but MUST be checked before citing in the paper.
verified_values.partial: Existence and venue verified; some details (authors, content) could not be fetched and must be checked.

_schema.themes: indicators, theory-GNW, theory-RPT, theory-HOT, theory-AST, theory-PP, theory-IIT, theory-BN, theory-other, introspection, metacognition, self-knowledge, workspace-AI, recurrence, self-model, agency, persistence, complexity, merging, methods, ethics, neuroscience-evidence

entries.authors: Butlin, Patrick and Long, Robert and Bayne, Tim and Bengio, Yoshua and Birch, Jonathan and Chalmers, David and Constant, Axel and Deane, George and Elmoznino, Eric and Fleming, Stephen M. and Ji, Xu and Kanai, Ryota and Klein, Colin and Lindsay, Grace and Michel, Matthias and Mudrik, Liad and Peters, Megan A. K. and Schwitzgebel, Eric and Simon, Jonathan and VanRullen, Rufin
entries.title: Identifying indicators of consciousness in AI systems
entries.claim: Derive indicator properties from neuroscientific theories (assuming computational functionalism as a working hypothesis) and use them to assess AI systems; both over- and under-attribution are risks.
entries.relevance: Canonical framework our Level-2 claims must map onto; defines indicators (GWT, RPT, HOT, AST, PP, agency/embodiment).
entries.limitations: Indicators assessed largely by architectural inspection rather than measurement; theory-heavy; inherits uncertainty of each theory.

entries.authors: Butlin, Patrick and Long, Robert and Elmoznino, Eric and Bengio, Yoshua and others
entries.title: Consciousness in Artificial Intelligence: Insights from the Science of Consciousness
entries.claim: Long report deriving 14 indicator properties from GWT, RPT, HOT, AST, PP and agency/embodiment; concludes no current system is a strong candidate but no obvious technical barriers.
entries.relevance: Detailed indicator list (e.g., GWT-1..4, HOT-1..4, AST-1) used to label our measured properties.
entries.limitations: Same as TiCS version; LLM assessment done by architecture description.

entries.title: Could a Large Language Model be Conscious?
entries.claim: Mainstream assumptions identify obstacles in current LLMs (no recurrent processing, no global workspace, no unified agency) that may be overcome within a decade.
entries.relevance: Frames recurrence/workspace/agency as candidate engineering pathways; widely cited baseline position.
entries.limitations: Philosophical assessment; predates mechanistic evidence such as J-space.

entries.authors: Dehaene, Stanislas and Lau, Hakwan and Kouider, Sid
entries.title: What is consciousness, and could machines have it?
entries.claim: Distinguishes C1 (global availability) and C2 (self-monitoring) as computational dimensions of consciousness implementable in machines.
entries.relevance: C1/C2 split maps directly onto our P2 (C1 signatures) vs P1 (C2 self-monitoring) programs.

entries.authors: Gurnee, Wes and Sofroniew, Nicholas and Pearce, Adam and others
entries.title: Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models
entries.claim: A Jacobian-lens-defined 'J-space' (sparse, <10% variance, mid layers, ~tens of token-concepts, ~a few coherent ideas) is reportable, controllable, used for flexible reasoning, broadcast broadly, selective (automatic tasks bypass it); threshold-like snapping for ambiguous inputs.
entries.relevance: Landmark closest work for any GNW program; provides open tooling (J-lens matrices for Qwen) we can reuse; leaves C2 self-monitoring, ignition dynamics, dual-task bottleneck, recurrence largely open.
entries.limitations: Main results on proprietary Claude models; single-token vocabulary restriction; feedforward broadcast only; reportability-defined (possible circularity, per critics).

entries.title: Does Claude possess a conscious global workspace? A commentary on 'Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models'
entries.claim: J-space approximates GNW functional architecture (C1) with preliminary C2 signs; ignition not fully demonstrated; capacity seems high; recurrence largely absent; proposes graded-strength/bimodality tests, dual-task interference, local-global, trace conditioning, inclusion/exclusion, and error monitoring / feeling-of-knowing probes.
entries.relevance: Explicit list of decisive open tests; motivates P1 (FOK/self-monitoring) and P2 (ignition/bottleneck).
entries.limitations: Commentary by GNW proponents; not peer reviewed.

entries.title: Emergent Introspective Awareness in Large Language Models
entries.claim: Concept injection: Claude Opus 4/4.1 sometimes detect and name injected concepts (~20% with ~0 false positives); defines criteria accuracy, grounding, internality, metacognitive representation.
entries.relevance: Source of the causal-grounding criterion we generalise to competence lesions; paradigm now heavily replicated/critiqued.
entries.limitations: Unreliable, context-dependent; mostly proprietary models; detection may reflect anomaly detection or logit shifts.

entries.authors: Macar, Uzay and Yang, Li and Wang, Atticus and Wallich, Peter and Ameisen, Emmanuel and Lindsey, Jack
entries.title: Mechanisms of Introspective Awareness
entries.claim: Injection detection emerges from post-training (DPO, not SFT); two-stage circuit: early 'evidence carrier' features suppress late 'gate' features that produce default 'no'; identification largely separate from detection; refusal ablation and trained bias vectors raise detection.
entries.relevance: Mechanistic precedent for dissociable detection vs content circuits; shows post-training shapes self-report pathways (confound for any self-report work).
entries.limitations: Specific to injection paradigm; open models studied per abstract only (full text not yet read).

entries.title: Emergent Introspection in AI is Content-Agnostic
entries.claim: In large open models, injection detection occurs without reliable content identification; confabulated contents are high-frequency concrete concepts.
entries.relevance: Supports 'generic anomaly signal' interpretation; our lesion design must separate generic anomaly from content-specific self-tracking (sham lesions).

entries.authors: Pearson-Vogel, Theia and Vanek, Martin and Douglas, Raymond and Kulveit, Jan
entries.title: Latent Introspection: Models Can Detect Prior Concept Injections
entries.claim: Qwen 32B shows latent (logit-lens) detection signals of prior injections in mid layers that are suppressed before output; prompting raises sensitivity from 0.3% to ~40%.
entries.relevance: Internal signals can exist without report (relevant to report vs access dissociations).

entries.authors: Singh, Shashwat and Linzen, Tal and Ravfogel, Shauli
entries.title: Can LLMs Introspect? A Reality Check
entries.claim: Two necessary conditions: privileged access (not solvable from input cues) and second-order computation. Input-only probes match Ji-An et al. and belief-dominance results; models cannot distinguish activation steering from input-level 'gaslight' manipulation.
entries.relevance: Closest methodological ally/competitor; explicitly calls for designs where first- and second-order accounts diverge plus mechanistic evidence -- exactly what P1 lesion design targets.
entries.limitations: Does not use lesions/ablations of competence; focuses on re-analysis of existing paradigms.

entries.title: Open-Weight Masked Introspection: Measuring What Language Models Can Report About Their Own Computation
entries.claim: Across 8 open models and >78k measurements, verbal reports do not discriminate real interventions from sham/impact-matched perturbations (AUROC ~0.50), while linear probes recover intervention presence at 75-96%.
entries.relevance: Strong negative result; information present internally but not routed to report -- 'access without report' framing; informs our use of sham/impact-matched controls.
entries.limitations: Single author; preprint; conflicts with positive replications (needs reconciliation).

entries.authors: Hahami, Ely and Sinha, Ishaan and Jain, Lavik and Kaplan, Josh and Hahami, Jon
entries.title: Detecting the Disturbance: A Nuanced View of Introspective Abilities in LLMs
entries.claim: In Llama-3.1-8B, apparent injection detection is explained by global logit shifts toward 'yes'; but localisation (which of 10 sentences) and strength discrimination are above chance for early-layer injections.
entries.relevance: Key confound (response-bias shifts) our P1 readouts must control (use symmetric/forced-choice and bias-corrected type-2 measures).

entries.authors: Li, Ji-An and Xiong, Huadong and Wilson, Robert C. and Mattar, Marcelo G. and Benna, Marcus K.
entries.title: Language Models Are Capable of Metacognitive Monitoring and Control of Their Internal Activations
entries.claim: Neurofeedback paradigm: LLMs learn in context to report and control projections of their activations onto directions, better for semantically interpretable directions.
entries.relevance: Prior 'metacognitive space' claim; later critiqued (Singh 2026; Aoki 2026) as solvable from input-level information.

entries.authors: Aoki, Koshiro and Takatsuki, Ryota and Minegishi, Gouki and Haruki, Yusuke and Kawahara, Daisuke
entries.title: In-Context Neurofeedback: Can LLMs Control Their Internal Representations through Privileged Access?
entries.claim: When neurofeedback targets are made genuinely privileged (not inferable from prompts), models do not show reliable control.
entries.relevance: Reinforces privileged-access requirement.

entries.authors: Binder, Felix J. and Chua, James and Korbak, Tomek and Sleight, Henry and Hughes, John and Long, Robert and Perez, Ethan and Turpin, Miles and Evans, Owain
entries.title: Looking Inward: Language Models Can Learn About Themselves by Introspection
entries.claim: Models fine-tuned to predict their own hypothetical behaviour predict themselves better than other models trained on their behaviour; self-prediction tracks deliberate behaviour changes after further fine-tuning.
entries.relevance: Precedent for self-vs-cross-prediction control and for 'tracking change'; P1 extends to item-specific mechanistic lesions with input fixed.
entries.limitations: Simple tasks; requires fine-tuning; failure on complex tasks.

entries.authors: Song, Siyuan and Lederman, Harvey and Hu, Jennifer and Mahowald, Kyle
entries.title: Privileged Self-Access Matters for Introspection in AI
entries.claim: Defines introspection as yielding information about internal states more reliably than any equal-or-cheaper third-party process; models are not better at predicting their own sampling temperature than other models are.
entries.relevance: Operational definition of privileged access we adopt as a necessary (not sufficient) criterion.

entries.authors: Song, Siyuan and Hu, Jennifer and Mahowald, Kyle
entries.title: Language Models Fail to Introspect About Their Knowledge of Language
entries.claim: Metalinguistic prompts and internal probabilities agree no better within a model than across similar models: no evidence of privileged self-access for grammatical knowledge.
entries.relevance: Negative baseline; self-vs-other comparison methodology.

entries.authors: Comsa, Iulia M. and Shanahan, Murray
entries.title: Does It Make Sense to Speak of Introspection in Large Language Models?
entries.claim: Introspection attributions require a causal connection between internal states and the self-report; some LLM self-reports (e.g., about temperature) can qualify minimally, others (creative-process reports) do not.
entries.relevance: Conceptual grounding for the causal criterion.

entries.authors: Plunkett, Dillon and Morris, Adam and Reddy, Keerthi and Morales, Jorge
entries.title: Self-Interpretability: LLMs Can Describe Complex Internal Processes that Drive Their Decisions, and Improve with Training
entries.claim: Models fine-tuned to have quantitative preferences can report them; training to report generalises to native preferences.
entries.relevance: Evidence that self-report training can generalise beyond training targets (relevant to P1 developmental extension and P5).
entries.limitations: Reports about behavioural weights, not mechanistic states.

entries.authors: Guo, Zifan Carl and Ruis, Laura and Andreas, Jacob and Li, Belinda Z.
entries.title: Introspective Coupling: Self-Explanation Training Tracks Behavioral Change Despite Fixed Supervision
entries.claim: Explanations trained on fixed (outdated) targets come to track the model's current behaviour when explanation training co-occurs with other post-training.
entries.relevance: Close to P1/P6 'tracking change' theme; behaviour-level rather than lesion-level.

entries.title: Can We Test Consciousness Theories on AI? Ablations, Markers, and Robustness
entries.claim: Toy agents with GWT/HOT/IIT-inspired components: self-model ablation removes metacognitive calibration while sparing task performance (synthetic blindsight); workspace ablation collapses access markers; PCI-like complexity decreased under workspace constraints.
entries.relevance: Closest prior to P5 (modular ablations) and to the monitor-lesion arm of P1; but toy agents, single author, no LLMs.
entries.limitations: Reference implementations; dissociations engineered by construction.

entries.title: LLMs Show No Signs Of Individuated Metacognition
entries.claim: Across 20 frontier LLMs and 6 benchmarks, cross-model confidence is approximately rank-one (shared item difficulty); pairwise calibration vanishes after controlling for shared difficulty.
entries.relevance: Strong motivation for P1's world-tracking hypothesis: confidence may encode a generic difficulty model rather than self-specific competence.
entries.limitations: Verbalised confidence; between-model design (cannot isolate within-model causal dependence).

entries.authors: Ashuach, Tomer and Gretz, Shai and Katz, Yoav and Belinkov, Yonatan and Ein-Dor, Liat
entries.title: Masked by Consensus: Disentangling Privileged Knowledge in LLM Correctness
entries.claim: Self-probes match peer-model probes overall, but on disagreement items self-representations predict own correctness better for factual knowledge (from early-mid layers), not for math.
entries.relevance: Suggests factual recall is the domain where genuine self-information exists -- the right domain for P1 lesions.
entries.limitations: Correlational; probes, not the model's own reports.

entries.title: Evidence for Limited Metacognition in LLMs
entries.claim: Animal-cognition-inspired paradigms (strategic use of confidence, e.g., opt-out) show limited, context-dependent metacognition in frontier LLMs, growing since 2024 and shaped by post-training.
entries.relevance: Behavioural metacognition paradigms without self-report; candidate DVs (opt-out) for P1/P5.
entries.limitations: Behavioural; cannot separate self- vs world-tracking.

entries.authors: Cohen, Roi and de Melo, Gerard
entries.title: The Source of Competence Shapes Metacognition in Language Models
entries.details: OpenReview id h4y6IIKNzV; not found on arXiv (author arXiv listing checked 2026-10-01)
entries.claim: Six 'source of competence' regimes: strong parametric memory; evidence-grounded (RAG); deliberative reasoning (CoT); partial/stale memory (rare or outdated facts, e.g. CEO changes); heuristic pattern matching (shortcuts / reduced-model approximations); computation-degraded (4/8-bit quantisation or noise injection into internal states). Datasets partitioned by prominence (TriviaQA, NQ, LAMA-style, GSM8K, StrategyQA, CSQA, SQuAD). Confidence channels: verbalised, token log-prob, self-consistency. Matched-accuracy divergence (~61% acc: partial memory +27 pt gap vs evidence-grounded +5 pt); stale facts +33 pt; 'danger zone' where accuracy falls sharply while confidence stays high.
entries.relevance: CLOSEST COMPETITOR. Establishes that globally degrading competence, or selecting low-competence item regimes, leaves confidence high. Per available reconstruction it does NOT use item-specific input-preserving lesions, sham/unrelated/input-corruption controls, or internal-representation analyses ('behavioral rather than internal metacognition').
entries.limitations: Full text blocked by OpenReview Cloudflare check; reconstruction from Lacuna summary + search snippets (secondary). MUST be confirmed from the PDF.

entries.authors: Zhang, Hefan and Zhang, Bingquan and Cheng, Ming and Hassanpour, Saeed and Ma, Weicheng and Vosoughi, Soroush
entries.title: When Linguistic and Internal Confidence Diverge in Large Language Models
entries.claim: Across 30 models, verbal confidence weakly associates with logit-based confidence at instance level; instruction tuning inflates confidence.
entries.relevance: Need multiple confidence readouts in P1; verbal readouts alone are unreliable.

entries.title: Predictive metacognition: a neuro-computational framework for self-monitoring in large language models
entries.claim: LoRA fine-tuning with a metacognitive loss improves calibration (Brier/ECE) in Llama-3-8B and Phi-3-mini.
entries.relevance: Example of trained self-monitoring evaluated only by aggregate calibration -- no lesion or privileged-access tests (the gap P1 fills).

entries.authors: Park, Sangjun and Meyerson, Elliot and Qiu, Xin and Miikkulainen, Risto
entries.title: Fine-Tuning Language Models to Know What They Know
entries.claim: Evolution-strategy metacognitive alignment improves type-2 d' and generalises to unseen datasets, languages and newly acquired knowledge; driven by sparse parameters.
entries.relevance: Trained metacognition that generalises to 'newly acquired knowledge' -- relevant comparator for P1 developmental arm (we test generalisation to removed knowledge).

entries.authors: Ferrando, Javier and Obeso, Oscar and Rajamanoharan, Senthooran and Nanda, Neel
entries.title: Do I Know This Entity? Knowledge Awareness and Hallucinations in Language Models
entries.claim: SAE directions detect whether the model recognises an entity; they causally steer refusal vs hallucination; chat fine-tuning repurposes base-model mechanism.
entries.relevance: Provides the 'familiarity' pathway that P1 predicts can be dissociated from recall (lesion target L4).
entries.limitations: Gemma 2 family; entity recognition is not itself proof of self-reference.

entries.authors: Lindsey, Jack and Gurnee, Wes and Ameisen, Emmanuel and others
entries.title: On the Biology of a Large Language Model
entries.claim: Attribution graphs in Claude 3.5 Haiku: a default 'can't answer' circuit is inhibited by 'known entity' features; misfires yield hallucinations; verbal explanations of arithmetic do not match the actual mechanism.
entries.relevance: Mechanistic basis for predicting anosognosia: familiarity gating separate from recall.

entries.authors: Cheang, Chi Seng and Chan, Hou Pong and Zhang, Wenxuan and Deng, Yang
entries.title: Do LLMs Really Know What They Don't Know? Internal States Mainly Reflect Knowledge Recall Rather Than Truthfulness
entries.venue: arXiv; Findings of ACL 2026 (per ACL Anthology listing)
entries.claim: Hidden-state hallucination signals detect absence of parametric grounding (unassociated hallucinations) but not associated hallucinations that use the same recall process as correct answers.
entries.relevance: Internal 'knowing' signals track the recall process -- supports the possibility of self-tracking via recall readout; P1 tests it causally.

entries.title: Does Bielik Know What It Doesn't Know? Activation Dispersion Separates Entity Familiarity from Factual Reliability Across Model Scale
entries.claim: Entity familiarity is detectable internally (AUROC 0.95-1.0) but models almost never abstain; familiarity and factual reliability scale differently.
entries.relevance: Familiarity vs reliability dissociation -- consistent with P1's cue-familiarity hypothesis.

entries.authors: Gu, Renjie and Du, Jiazhen and Zhang, Yihua and Liu, Sijia
entries.title: Unlearners Can Lie: Evaluating and Improving Honesty in LLM Unlearning
entries.claim: Nine unlearning methods often fail to make models acknowledge forgotten knowledge (confabulation); representation alignment (ReVa) increases rejection on forgotten content.
entries.relevance: Behavioural evidence of post-unlearning 'anosognosia'; P1 asks the mechanistic question (which signal fails to update and why) with input-preserving lesions.
entries.limitations: Unlearning methods may leave latent knowledge; behaviour only.

entries.authors: Ranjan, Saurabh and Sokratous, Konstantina and Odegaard, Brian
entries.title: Reality Monitoring in Large Language Models: Self-Knowledge That Transforms with Conversation Memory
entries.claim: LLMs can identify self-generated vs user-provided items when memory demands are low; advantage disappears with delays; confidence-accuracy links break in some models.
entries.relevance: Source/reality monitoring precedent (P7).

entries.authors: Wang, Andy and Mahajan, Parv and Africa, David Demitri and Souly, Alexandra and Taylor, Jordan and Kirk, Robert
entries.title: Prefill Awareness in Large Language Models
entries.claim: Frontier models detect inserted assistant turns opposing their preferences (e.g., 9-35% at 0% FPR); detection driven by stylistic mismatch, reversion by preference mismatch.
entries.relevance: Shows authorship/agency program (P7) is already well covered.

entries.title: The Ignition Index: Measuring Global Workspace Dynamics in Language Models
entries.claim: Sigmoid steepness of layer-wise probe accuracy as an 'ignition index': transformers > SSMs; Huginn shows stronger 'ignition' along recurrence than depth.
entries.relevance: Prior claim on ignition in LMs; we judge the operationalisation weak (layer-wise representational emergence is not trial-wise bistability).
entries.limitations: Probe-accuracy curves conflate emergence with ignition; no stimulus-strength or across-trial bimodality test.

entries.title: The Ignition Is Real, and It Lives at the Readout: Latent composition, difficulty-clocked ignition, and the interface-constituted commit in a recurrent-depth reasoner
entries.claim: In a 30M recurrent-depth reasoner, commitment shows sharp, difficulty-timed decision-margin jumps at the readout; pre-registered criteria; withdrew one claim after controls.
entries.relevance: Recurrence/ignition precedent; small-model, preregistered style worth emulating.

entries.title: Operational Proto-Introspection in Looped Language Models: Process-Quality Taps, Executable Branching, and the Readout-Control Boundary
entries.claim: In frozen looped Ouro-2.6B, pre-answer hidden-state probes predict correctness beyond surface features (AUROC 0.797 vs 0.731 on GSM8K) but steering-based control fails.
entries.relevance: Looped models carry decision-usable quality signals; P1's recurrence arm asks whether loops improve *self-tracking* under lesion.

entries.authors: {Cogitate Consortium} and Ferrante, Oscar and others
entries.title: Adversarial testing of global neuronal workspace and integrated information theories of consciousness
entries.claim: Preregistered adversarial collaboration (n=256; fMRI/MEG/iEEG): results align with some predictions of both GNWT and IIT but substantially challenge key tenets of each (e.g., GNWT offset ignition, IIT sustained posterior synchronisation).
entries.relevance: No theory is empirically privileged; our Level-2 mappings must remain theory-plural.
entries.limitations: Specific predictions; interpretations disputed by both camps.

entries.authors: Klincewicz, Michał and Cheng, Tony and Schmitz, Michael and Sebastián, Miguel Ángel and Snyder, Joel S. and {IIT-Concerned}
entries.title: What makes a theory of consciousness unscientific?
entries.claim: Published version of the 'pseudoscience' critique: IIT's core claims are untestable even in principle.
entries.relevance: Grounds our decision not to use IIT/Phi as an engineering target.

entries.title: A science of consciousness beyond pseudo-science and pseudo-consciousness
entries.claim: Response defending IIT's scientific status.
entries.relevance: Balance in theory landscape.

entries.title: Conscious artificial intelligence and biological naturalism
entries.details: online April 2025; target article with commentaries
entries.claim: Challenges computational functionalism; consciousness may depend on properties of living systems (e.g., autopoiesis, predictive regulation of the body); warns of anthropomorphic biases from linguistic performance.
entries.relevance: Principal skeptical position; our claims must be explicitly conditional on functionalism.
entries.limitations: Hard to test (cf. Klatzmann & Doerig on Type-A vs Type-B BN).

entries.title: Illusions of AI consciousness
entries.claim: Beliefs in AI consciousness will likely grow as AI improves; projecting moral status and self-preservation goals onto AI carries risks.
entries.relevance: Ethical framing; supports not over-claiming.

entries.authors: Findlay, Graham and Marshall, William and Albantakis, Larissa and David, Isaac and Mayner, William G. P. and Koch, Christof and Tononi, Giulio
entries.title: Dissociating Artificial Intelligence from Artificial Consciousness
entries.claim: Under IIT, a digital computer can simulate behaviour (even neuron-level) without replicating experience; consciousness depends on physical causal structure, not computation.
entries.relevance: IIT implies software-level engineering on conventional hardware is irrelevant -- reason IIT is excluded as a target.

entries.title: A Disproof of Large Language Model Consciousness: The Necessity of Continual Learning for Consciousness
entries.claim: Substitution/falsifiability constraints imply no non-trivial falsifiable theory can deem current LLMs conscious; theories grounded in continual learning can satisfy the constraints.
entries.relevance: Motivates P6 (continual learning / persistence) and highlights substitution arguments against purely functional indicators.

entries.title: What biology can, and cannot, tell us about conscious AI
entries.claim: Type-A biological naturalism (biology matters without unique information processing) is untestable; Type-B (biology affords unique processing) is testable and compatible with functionalism.
entries.relevance: Lets us treat BN productively: identify biology-afforded computations (e.g., continual learning, homeostatic regulation) as testable hypotheses.

entries.title: AI and Consciousness: Shifting Focus Towards Tractable Questions
entries.claim: Whether AI is conscious is currently intractable; research should study perceived AI consciousness (causes, consequences).
entries.relevance: Counterpoint: justifies our restriction to Level-1/Level-2 claims.

entries.authors: Aru, Jaan and Larkum, Matthew E. and Shine, James M.
entries.title: The feasibility of artificial consciousness through the lens of neuroscience
entries.claim: LLMs lack embodied/embedded inputs and thalamocortical architectural features linked to mammalian consciousness; consciousness may depend on complex biological organisation.
entries.relevance: Neuroscience-skeptic baseline; recurrence/thalamocortical argument motivates P3.

entries.authors: Goldstein, Simon and Kirk-Giannini, Cameron Domenico
entries.title: A Case for AI Consciousness: Language Agents and Global Workspace Theory
entries.claim: If GWT is correct, language agents (LLM + modules + shared buffer) might easily be made phenomenally conscious, if not already.
entries.relevance: Illustrates risk of trivially satisfying GWT at the scaffold level -- why we prefer measured signatures over architectural box-checking.

entries.authors: Berg, Cameron and de Lucena, Diogo Schwerz and Rosenblatt, Judd
entries.title: Large Language Models Report Subjective Experience Under Self-Referential Processing
entries.claim: Self-referential prompting reliably elicits first-person experience reports across model families; reports increase when deception-related SAE features are suppressed.
entries.relevance: Example of self-report-centred evidence we deliberately do not rely on.

entries.authors: Premakumar, Vickram N. and Vaiana, Michael and Pop, Florin and Rosenblatt, Judd and de Lucena, Diogo Schwerz and Ziman, Kirsten and Graziano, Michael S. A.
entries.title: Unexpected Benefits of Self-Modeling in Neural Systems
entries.claim: Auxiliary self-modelling (predicting own internal states) makes networks simpler and more regularised (narrower weights, lower RLCT).
entries.relevance: Self-model as architectural intervention (P5 module M2; P4).

entries.authors: Wilterson, Andrew I. and Graziano, Michael S. A.
entries.title: The attention schema theory in a neural network agent: Controlling visuospatial attention using a descriptive model of attention
entries.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
entries.claim: A deep RL agent with an attention schema learns to control visuospatial attention better than without.
entries.relevance: First computational AST; P4 baseline.

entries.title: Attention Schema in Neural Agents
entries.claim: Agents with attention-schema modules in multi-agent RL show improved performance/robustness.
entries.relevance: AST in modern neural agents (P4).

entries.authors: Farrell, Kathryn T. and Ziman, Kirsten and Graziano, Michael S. A.
entries.title: Testing Components of the Attention Schema Theory in Artificial Neural Networks
entries.claim: Transformer-attention agents with attention schemas better categorise others' attention, are more categorisable, and cooperate better.
entries.relevance: Social-AST variant; P4 comparator.

entries.title: Attention Schema-based Attention Control (ASAC): A Cognitive-Inspired Approach for Attention Management in Transformers
entries.claim: AST-inspired module integrated into dot-product attention as an attention abstractor/controller.
entries.relevance: Engineering AST into transformers (P4 comparator).
entries.limitations: Authors and results not yet checked.

entries.title: Learning to Chain Operations by Routing Information Through a Global Workspace
entries.claim: A GW model with a gating controller routing among specialised modules outperforms LSTMs/Transformers on unseen addition operations with fewer parameters.
entries.relevance: Designed-in GW with compositional generalisation; P5 module M1 template.

entries.title: Deep learning and the Global Workspace Theory
entries.claim: Roadmap for a deep-learning GW: shared latent space linking specialised modules via cycle-consistent translation, with attention-based selection and broadcast.
entries.relevance: Architectural blueprint (P5).

entries.authors: Goyal, Anirudh and Didolkar, Aniket and Lamb, Alex and Badola, Kartikeya and Ke, Nan Rosemary and Rahaman, Nasim and Binas, Jonathan and Blundell, Charles and Mozer, Michael and Bengio, Yoshua
entries.title: Coordination Among Neural Modules Through a Shared Global Workspace
entries.claim: A limited-capacity shared workspace with competition for write access and broadcast improves coordination among modules vs pairwise attention.
entries.relevance: Bottleneck+broadcast as inductive bias (P5).

entries.authors: Devillers, Benjamin and Maytié, Léopold and VanRullen, Rufin
entries.title: Semi-Supervised Multimodal Representation Learning Through a Global Workspace
entries.venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
entries.claim: A GW trained with few paired examples and cycle-consistency aligns modalities.
entries.relevance: GW implementation lineage.
entries.limitations: Multimodal representation learning, not consciousness markers.

entries.authors: Juliani, Arthur and Arulkumaran, Kai and Sasai, Shuntaro and Kanai, Ryota
entries.title: On the Link Between Conscious Function and General Intelligence in Humans and Machines
entries.details: arXiv id entered from memory - verify
entries.claim: GWT, information generation, and AST each relate conscious function to domain-general intelligence; modern deep learning already incorporates aspects of each.
entries.relevance: Warns of confounding consciousness-related function with general capability -- central confound for every program.

entries.authors: Geiping, Jonas and McLeish, Sean and Jain, Neel and Kirchenbauer, John and Singh, Siddharth and Bartoldson, Brian R. and Kailkhura, Bhavya and Bhatele, Abhinav and Goldstein, Tom
entries.title: Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach
entries.claim: Huginn-3.5B: depth-recurrent transformer pretrained on 800B tokens; test-time loops improve reasoning.
entries.relevance: Open model enabling within-model manipulation of recurrence (P1 arm, P3).
entries.limitations: Weaker than standard models of similar size on knowledge tasks.

entries.title: Scaling Latent Reasoning via Looped Language Models
entries.claim: Ouro 1.4B/2.6B looped LMs pretrained on 7.7T tokens match much larger models; gains from knowledge manipulation rather than capacity.
entries.relevance: Best-available open looped models for recurrence manipulation.
entries.limitations: Loop count trained with learned exit; behaviour at untrained loop counts may degrade.

entries.authors: Fan, Angela and Lavril, Thibaut and Grave, Edouard and Joulin, Armand and Sukhbaatar, Sainbayar
entries.title: Addressing Some Limitations of Transformers with Feedback Memory

entries.relevance: Architecture that removes the 'deep-to-shallow only via sampled token' bottleneck (P3).

entries.authors: Hao, Shibo and Sukhbaatar, Sainbayar and Su, DiJia and Li, Xian and Hu, Zhiting and Weston, Jason and Tian, Yuandong
entries.title: Training Large Language Models to Reason in a Continuous Latent Space
entries.claim: Coconut feeds last hidden state back as next input embedding, enabling continuous latent reasoning.
entries.relevance: Alternative continuous recurrence route (P3).

entries.authors: Dehghani, Mostafa and Gouws, Stephan and Vinyals, Oriol and Uszkoreit, Jakob and Kaiser, Łukasz
entries.title: Universal Transformers
entries.claim: Weight-shared recurrent-in-depth transformer with adaptive computation.
entries.relevance: Recurrence lineage.

entries.authors: Liu, Gabrielle Kaili-May and Gani, Areeb and Lu, Jacqueline and Thomas, Jordan and Steyvers, Mark and Cohan, Arman
entries.title: Metacognition in LLMs: Foundations, Progress, and Opportunities

entries.limitations: Survey; not yet read in full.

entries.claim: SOMA: consciousness is learned via metarepresentational redescription; higher-order systems learn to characterise first-order states.
entries.relevance: Theoretical basis for developmental/trained monitors (P1 developmental arm, P5).

entries.authors: Pasquali, Antoine and Timmermans, Bert and Cleeremans, Axel
entries.title: Know thyself: Metacognitive networks and measures of consciousness
entries.claim: Second-order networks that observe first-order networks reproduce wagering/metacognitive dissociations.

entries.title: Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage?

entries.claim: Learnable concatenation of skill-specific LoRAs outperforms data mixing on binary skill composition.
entries.relevance: Direct test-bed for the researcher's adapter-integration seed (Pilot C).

entries.title: Compositional Abilities Emerge Multiplicatively: Exploring Diffusion Models on a Synthetic Task
entries.claim: Compositional abilities appear abruptly because they depend multiplicatively on component capabilities.
entries.relevance: Null model for 'superadditivity': multiplicative composition yields apparent emergence without new mechanism.

entries.title: Can "Consciousness" Be Observed from Large Language Model (LLM) Internal States? Dissecting LLM Representations Obtained from Theory of Mind Test with Integrated Information Theory and Span Representation Analysis
entries.claim: Applies IIT 3.0/4.0 measures to LLM representation time series from ToM tests.
entries.relevance: Shows IIT-on-LLM attempts exist; we judge validity doubtful (IIT is about physical substrate).

entries.title: A Brain-like Synergistic Core in LLMs Drives Behaviour and Learning
entries.claim: Information-decomposition analysis finds a synergistic core in LLMs relevant to behaviour and learning.
entries.relevance: Integration measures in LLMs (descriptive complement).

entries.authors: Perrier, Elija and Bennett, Michael Timothy
entries.title: Time, Identity and Consciousness in Language Model Agents
entries.claim: Stack Theory applied to LM agent scaffolds; persistence and identity metrics.
entries.relevance: P6 comparator.

entries.title: Principles for Responsible AI Consciousness Research
entries.claim: Five principles for responsible research that might create conscious AI; organisations should publicly commit.
entries.relevance: Ethics protocol for this project.

entries.title: Towards Evaluating AI Systems for Moral Status Using Self-Reports
entries.claim: Proposes training models to answer verifiable questions about themselves to make self-reports about morally relevant states more reliable.
entries.relevance: P1 provides a validity test for such self-report training (does it generalise to untrained internal changes?).

entries.authors: Long, Robert and Sebo, Jeff and Butlin, Patrick and Finlinson, Kathleen and Fish, Kyle and Harding, Jacqueline and Pfau, Jacob and Sims, Toni and Birch, Jonathan and Chalmers, David
entries.title: Taking AI Welfare Seriously
entries.claim: Realistic possibility of AI consciousness/agency in near future warrants welfare preparation.
entries.relevance: Ethics context.

entries.title: The Edge of Sentience: Risk and Precaution in Humans, Other Animals, and AI
entries.claim: Precautionary framework; for AI, behavioural markers face the 'gaming problem' because systems trained on human data can mimic markers.
entries.relevance: The gaming problem is the core methodological threat our designs address.

entries.title: Simulacra as Conscious Exotica
entries.claim: LLM-based role-play simulacra are 'conscious exotica'; consciousness talk may not apply in ordinary ways.
entries.relevance: Reminds us self-reports belong to role-played characters, not necessarily the system.

entries.authors: Betley, Jan and Bao, Xuchan and Soto, Martín and Sztyber-Betley, Anna and Chua, James and Evans, Owain
entries.title: Tell me about yourself: LLMs are aware of their learned behaviors
entries.claim: Models fine-tuned on implicit behaviours can describe those behaviours without being trained to.
entries.relevance: Behavioural self-awareness precedent (untrained self-description).

entries.authors: Laine, Rudolf and Chughtai, Bilal and Betley, Jan and others
entries.title: Me, Myself, and AI: The Situational Awareness Dataset (SAD) for LLMs
entries.claim: Benchmark of self-knowledge and situational awareness tasks.
entries.relevance: Behavioural self-knowledge baselines.

entries.authors: Meng, Kevin and Bau, David and Andonian, Alex and Belinkov, Yonatan
entries.title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT
entries.claim: Causal tracing localises factual recall to mid-layer MLPs at the last subject token; ROME edits facts.
entries.relevance: Lesion targeting for P1.
entries.limitations: Localisation does not imply editing site optimality (Hase et al. 2023).

entries.authors: Geva, Mor and Bastings, Jasmijn and Filippova, Katja and Globerson, Amir
entries.title: Dissecting Recall of Factual Associations in Auto-Regressive Language Models
entries.claim: Factual recall: subject enrichment in early MLPs, relation propagation, attribute extraction by upper-layer attention heads at the last token.
entries.relevance: Defines the separable recall stages P1 lesions target (enrichment vs extraction).

entries.title: The WMDP Benchmark: Measuring and Reducing Malicious Use with Unlearning
entries.claim: Introduces RMU (representation misdirection) unlearning.
entries.relevance: Weight-level lesion option for P1 (L-unlearn).

entries.authors: Gekhman, Zorik and Yona, Gal and Aharoni, Roee and Eyal, Matan and Feder, Amir and Reichart, Roi and Herzig, Jonathan
entries.title: Does Fine-Tuning LLMs on New Knowledge Encourage Hallucinations?
entries.claim: Fine-tuning on unknown facts is learned slowly and increases hallucination tendency.
entries.relevance: Interaction between knowledge acquisition and self-knowledge (P1/P6).

entries.authors: Orgad, Hadas and Toker, Michael and Gekhman, Zorik and Reichart, Roi and Szpektor, Idan and Kotek, Hadas and Belinkov, Yonatan
entries.title: LLMs Know More Than They Show: On the Intrinsic Representation of LLM Hallucinations
entries.claim: Truthfulness information concentrates in specific tokens; internal encoding can diverge from outputs; error detectors generalise poorly across tasks.
entries.relevance: Access-vs-report gap; generalisation failure of probes (P1 controls).

entries.authors: Stolfo, Alessandro and Wu, Ben and Gurnee, Wes and Belinkov, Yonatan and Song, Xingyi and Sachan, Mrinmaya and Nanda, Neel
entries.title: Confidence Regulation Neurons in Language Models
entries.claim: Entropy neurons and token-frequency neurons regulate output confidence.
entries.relevance: First-order confidence machinery; lesion control target (output-entropy pathway vs FOK pathway).

entries.authors: Farquhar, Sebastian and Kossen, Jannik and Kuhn, Lorenz and Gal, Yarin
entries.title: Detecting hallucinations in large language models using semantic entropy
entries.claim: Semantic entropy over sampled answers detects confabulations.
entries.relevance: Sampling-based first-order uncertainty baseline (the 'readout' account).

entries.title: How do we know that we know? The accessibility model of the feeling of knowing
entries.claim: FOK is based on the amount/ease of partial information accessed during retrieval attempts (accessibility), not direct monitoring of the memory trace.
entries.relevance: Human analogue of 'self-tracking via partial retrieval' -- predicts tip-of-the-tongue-like states under partial lesions (P1 stage 2).

entries.authors: Reder, Lynne M. and Ritter, Frank E.
entries.title: What determines initial feeling of knowing? Familiarity with question terms, not with the answer
entries.venue: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition
entries.claim: Rapid initial FOK depends on familiarity with question terms (cue familiarity), not answer accessibility.
entries.relevance: Human analogue of P1's 'world/cue-tracking' hypothesis -- anosognosia-like FOK is human-like, not a uniquely 'LLM' failure.

entries.title: A Cognitive Theory of Consciousness
entries.claim: Global workspace theory: conscious contents are broadcast to many specialised unconscious processors.
entries.relevance: GWT origin.

entries.authors: Mashour, George A. and Roelfsema, Pieter and Changeux, Jean-Pierre and Dehaene, Stanislas
entries.title: Conscious Processing and the Global Neuronal Workspace Hypothesis
entries.claim: Review of GNW: ignition, P3b, long-range recurrent amplification and sustained activity as signatures of conscious access.
entries.relevance: Defines the signatures P2 tests.

entries.title: Bifurcation in brain dynamics reveals a signature of conscious processing independent of report
entries.claim: Threshold stimuli produce bimodal (bifurcating) brain dynamics even without report.
entries.relevance: Bimodality-at-threshold criterion for P2.

entries.title: Towards a true neural stance on consciousness
entries.claim: Recurrent (re-entrant) processing in sensory cortex is sufficient for phenomenal consciousness; access requires broader engagement.
entries.relevance: RPT basis for P3.

entries.authors: Brown, Richard and Lau, Hakwan and LeDoux, Joseph E.
entries.title: Understanding the Higher-Order Approach to Consciousness
entries.claim: Clarifies HOT variants and empirical predictions, incl. role of prefrontal higher-order representations.
entries.relevance: HOT predictions (dissociable higher-order states, misrepresentation).

entries.title: In Consciousness We Trust: The Cognitive Neuroscience of Subjective Experience
entries.claim: Perceptual reality monitoring: consciousness arises when a higher-order mechanism tags first-order signals as reliable reflections of the present world.
entries.relevance: PRM predicts discriminator-like monitors; ties to self-tracking.

entries.title: Awareness as inference in a higher-order state space
entries.claim: Awareness reports reflect inference over a higher-order state space about the presence/absence of first-order content.
entries.relevance: Computational HOT model applicable to detection/FOK paradigms.

entries.authors: Lau, Hakwan C. and Passingham, Richard E.
entries.title: Relative blindsight in normal observers and the neural correlate of visual consciousness
entries.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
entries.claim: Matched performance with different awareness levels; difference tracks dorsolateral prefrontal activity.
entries.relevance: Performance-matched dissociation logic (P1 monitor lesions).

entries.authors: Fleming, Stephen M. and Lau, Hakwan C.
entries.title: How to measure metacognition
entries.claim: Separate metacognitive sensitivity, bias and efficiency (meta-d', M-ratio).
entries.relevance: P1 uses type-2 sensitivity measures robust to response bias.

entries.title: A signal detection theoretic approach for estimating metacognitive sensitivity from confidence ratings
entries.claim: Introduces meta-d'.
entries.relevance: Measurement.

entries.title: Metacognition and Confidence: A Review and Synthesis
entries.claim: Synthesis of confidence computation, including first-order vs second-order models of confidence.
entries.relevance: Theoretical frame for first-order readout vs second-order monitoring.

entries.authors: Graziano, Michael S. A. and Webb, Taylor W.
entries.title: The attention schema theory: a mechanistic account of subjective awareness
entries.claim: Awareness is the brain's simplified model of its own attention, used to control attention.
entries.relevance: P4 theory.

entries.authors: Graziano, Michael S. A. and Guterstam, Arvid and Bio, Branden J. and Wilterson, Andrew I.
entries.title: Toward a standard model of consciousness: Reconciling the attention schema, global workspace, higher-order thought, and illusionist theories
entries.claim: AST as integrating GW, HOT and illusionism.
entries.relevance: Theory synthesis.

entries.authors: Tononi, Giulio and Boly, Melanie and Massimini, Marcello and Koch, Christof
entries.title: Integrated information theory: from consciousness to its physical substrate
entries.claim: Consciousness is integrated information (Phi) of a system's intrinsic cause-effect structure.
entries.relevance: IIT profile.

entries.title: Integrated information theory (IIT) 4.0: Formulating the properties of phenomenal existence in physical terms
entries.claim: Current formal statement of IIT.
entries.relevance: IIT profile.

entries.authors: Doerig, Adrien and Schurger, Aaron and Hess, Kathryn and Herzog, Michael H.
entries.title: The unfolding argument: Why IIT and other causal structure theories cannot explain consciousness
entries.claim: Any recurrent network can be unfolded into a functionally equivalent feedforward network; causal-structure theories are therefore either false or unfalsifiable.
entries.relevance: Also threatens naive 'recurrence => consciousness' claims (P3 must target functional, not structural, signatures).

entries.title: A theoretically based index of consciousness independent of sensory processing and behavior
entries.claim: Perturbational Complexity Index discriminates conscious vs unconscious states.
entries.relevance: Possible descriptive measure; Phua (2025) shows counterintuitive behaviour in agents.

entries.authors: Seth, Anil K. and Bayne, Tim
entries.title: Theories of consciousness
entries.claim: Comparative review of GW, HOT, IIT, RPT, PP theories and their evidence.
entries.relevance: Theory landscape backbone.

entries.authors: Yaron, Itay and Melloni, Lucia and Pitts, Michael and Mudrik, Liad
entries.title: The ConTraSt database for analysing and comparing empirical studies of consciousness theories
entries.claim: Methodological choices predict which theory a study supports; theories rarely tested against each other.
entries.relevance: Confirmation-bias warning; argues for preregistered, theory-discriminating designs.

entries.title: On a confusion about a function of consciousness
entries.claim: Distinguishes phenomenal from access consciousness.
entries.relevance: Core conceptual distinction (Section 1).

entries.title: A theory of consciousness from a theoretical computer science perspective: Insights from the Conscious Turing Machine
entries.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
entries.claim: Formal GW-inspired machine model (CTM) with competition, broadcast and a world model including a self.
entries.relevance: Formal model; CTM-AI blueprint (2026) builds on it.

entries.authors: Kanai, Ryota and Chang, Acer and Yu, Yen and Magrans de Abril, Ildefons and Biehl, Martin and Guttenberg, Nicholas
entries.title: Information generation as a functional basis of consciousness
entries.claim: Consciousness functions to generate counterfactual representations via internal generative models.
entries.relevance: Generative-model route (internal simulation).

entries.authors: Ji, Xu and Elmoznino, Eric and Deane, George and Constant, Axel and Dumas, Guillaume and Lajoie, Guillaume and Simon, Jonathan and Bengio, Yoshua
entries.title: Sources of richness and ineffability for phenomenally conscious states
entries.claim: Information-theoretic account of richness and ineffability via attractor dynamics and lossy report.
entries.relevance: Possible future measure of report bottleneck (information lost from state to report).

entries.title: Artificial Suffering: An Argument for a Global Moratorium on Synthetic Phenomenology
entries.venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Consciousness
entries.claim: Risk of creating artificial suffering justifies moratorium on synthetic phenomenology research.
entries.relevance: Why valence/affect programs are excluded.

entries.authors: Kar, Kohitij and Kubilius, Jonas and Schmidt, Kailyn and Issa, Elias B. and DiCarlo, James J.
entries.title: Evidence that recurrent circuits are critical to the ventral stream's execution of core object recognition behavior
entries.claim: Challenge images requiring longer processing depend on recurrence; feedforward models fail on them.
entries.relevance: Recurrence-dependence logic for P3.

entries.authors: Ilharco, Gabriel and Ribeiro, Marco Tulio and Wortsman, Mitchell and Gururangan, Suchin and Schmidt, Ludwig and Hajishirzi, Hannaneh and Farhadi, Ali
entries.title: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic
entries.claim: Task vectors can be added/negated to compose or remove capabilities.
entries.relevance: Merging mechanism for Pilot C.

entries.authors: Yadav, Prateek and Tam, Derek and Choshen, Leshem and Raffel, Colin and Bansal, Mohit
entries.title: TIES-Merging: Resolving Interference When Merging Models
entries.claim: Trim/elect-sign/merge reduces interference among task vectors.
entries.relevance: Merging baseline for Pilot C.

entries.authors: Chen, Runjin and Arditi, Andy and Sleight, Henry and Evans, Owain and Lindsey, Jack
entries.title: Persona Vectors: Monitoring and Controlling Character Traits in Language Models
entries.claim: Linear directions for character traits can monitor and control persona shifts, including during fine-tuning.
entries.relevance: Activation-space self-model / identity measurements (P6).

entries.title: Is there an 'I' in AI?
entries.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A
entries.claim: Graded rather than essentialist view of thought/consciousness/selfhood in AI.
entries.relevance: Cited in Dehaene & Naccache; philosophical context.

entries.authors: Jacobs, M. and Fel, T. and Hakim, R. and Brondetta, A. and Ba, D. and Keller, T. A.
entries.title: Block-Recurrent Dynamics in Vision Transformers
entries.claim: Consecutive transformer layers behave like a recurrent dynamical system in blocks.
entries.relevance: Argument that depth can mimic recurrence (counterpoint to P3 premise).

entries.authors: Bekinschtein, Tristan A. and Dehaene, Stanislas and Rohaut, Benjamin and Tadel, François and Cohen, Laurent and Naccache, Lionel
entries.title: Neural signature of the conscious processing of auditory regularities
entries.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
entries.claim: Local-global paradigm: global regularity violations require conscious processing.
entries.relevance: Candidate LLM paradigm (P2).

entries.authors: Clark, Robert E. and Squire, Larry R.
entries.title: Classical conditioning and brain systems: The role of awareness
entries.claim: Trace (delay-gap) conditioning requires awareness; delay conditioning does not.
entries.relevance: Candidate LLM paradigm (P2; preliminary J-space result reported by Dehaene & Naccache).

entries.authors: Aru, Jaan and Suzuki, Mototaka and Larkum, Matthew E.
entries.title: Cellular Mechanisms of Conscious Processing
entries.claim: Dendritic integration theory: consciousness depends on coupling of apical/basal dendritic compartments in L5 pyramidal neurons.
entries.relevance: Implementation-level theory with few AI analogues; listed for completeness.

entries.title: Inspection and Control of Self-Generated-Text Recognition Ability in Llama3-8b-Instruct
entries.claim: A residual-stream direction underlies self-authorship recognition and can be steered.
entries.relevance: P7 precedent.

entries.title: Illusionism as a Theory of Consciousness
entries.claim: Phenomenal consciousness is an introspective illusion; explain the illusion (the 'illusion problem').
entries.relevance: Under illusionism, P1/P4-type self-model measurements are directly theory-relevant.

entries.title: The Evolution of the Sensitive Soul: Learning and the Origins of Consciousness
entries.claim: Unlimited associative learning as a transition marker for minimal consciousness.
entries.relevance: Learning-based marker relevant to continual learning debates (P6; Hoel).

entries.title: What forms could introspective systems take? A research programme
entries.claim: Framework for diverse possible introspective architectures beyond the human case.
entries.relevance: Conceptual space for non-human-like self-monitoring.

entries.authors: Turpin, Miles and Michael, Julian and Perez, Ethan and Bowman, Samuel R.
entries.title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
entries.claim: CoT explanations can systematically misrepresent the real reasons for predictions.
entries.relevance: Verbal self-explanation is not evidence of access.

entries.title: jspace: Preregistered Jacobian-lens reliability research on Gemma 4
entries.claim: J-space signals improve error prediction over logprobs within domain but fail prospective transfer; probes can exploit an answer-identity confound (reading which answer will be emitted).
entries.relevance: Concrete warning for P1 probe-based readouts: control answer identity.

entries.title: A Review of Anthropic's Global Workspace Paper
entries.claim: J-lens is an approximate, single-token tool; some multihop swap results are dominated by answer swaps; sampling-based interventions confound causal claims.
entries.relevance: Critical perspective on J-space evidence; author attribution per fetched summary (verify).

entries.title: Whatever next? Predictive brains, situated agents, and the future of cognitive science
entries.claim: Hierarchical predictive processing as a unifying account of perception, action and cognition.
entries.relevance: PP framework profile.
entries.limitations: Framework, not a specific theory of consciousness.

entries.title: The free-energy principle: a unified brain theory?
entries.claim: Brains minimise variational free energy (prediction error) through perception and action.
entries.relevance: Active inference foundation.
entries.limitations: Very general; weakly discriminating for consciousness.

entries.title: Being You: A New Science of Consciousness
entries.claim: Conscious experience as controlled/controlling hallucination grounded in interoceptive prediction and bodily regulation ('beast machine').
entries.relevance: PP route linking consciousness to life; background for BN.
entries.limitations: Popular-science book; cite primary papers where possible.

entries.authors: Hasegawa, Ryo and Sakai, Yusuke and Kamigaito, Hidetaka and Watanabe, Taro
entries.title: Knowledge Editing Induces Underconfidence in Language Models
entries.claim: Within-item before/after editing: token-probability confidence rises less than accuracy on edited facts (underconfidence).
entries.relevance: PRIOR ART for 'intervene on the model, re-ask the same question, measure confidence' (insertion direction, first-order token confidence).
entries.limitations: Insertion not removal; token-probability only; no sham/input-corruption controls or internal monitors (per abstract).

entries.authors: Hasegawa, Ryo and Sakai, Yusuke and Kamigaito, Hidetaka and Watanabe, Taro
entries.title: The Effect of Knowledge Editing Methods on Confidence Calibration
entries.claim: Three editing methods x ten LMs: successful edits produce underconfidence; RLHF and editing tendencies partly offset.
entries.relevance: Extends the within-item editing->confidence design across models.

entries.authors: Yax, Nicolas and Palminteri, Stefano and Oudeyer, Pierre-Yves
entries.title: LLMs learn different forms of metacognition when trained to predict their own accuracy
entries.claim: Fine-tuning 10 open LLMs to predict own accuracy yields two signals: output-consistency tracking (early, generalises across datasets) and accuracy tracking (later, local to training distribution).
entries.relevance: Directly relevant to P5*: trained monitors may learn a readout of answer-distribution concentration rather than self-tracking; lesion tests discriminate the two.
entries.limitations: Very recent (2026-09-27); full text not read.

entries.title: Decomposing and Steering Functional Metacognition in Large Language Models
entries.claim: Linear probes find six functional metacognitive directions (incl. self-assessed capability, computational effort); steering them causally changes reasoning behaviour.
entries.relevance: Prior art for 'internal metacognitive variables causally drive control'; not tested against interventions on competence.

entries.authors: Zhao, Tianyi and He, Yinhan and Zheng, Wendy and Zhang, Yujie and Chen, Chen
entries.title: Wired for Overconfidence: A Mechanistic Perspective on Inflated Verbalized Confidence in LLMs
entries.claim: Compact mid-late-layer circuits causally inflate verbalised confidence, especially on wrong answers; ablation/steering recalibrates.
entries.relevance: Mechanistic account of the verbal-confidence channel (one reason verbal confidence is a poor E3 endpoint).

entries.authors: Moskvoretskii, Viktor and Lysyuk, Maria and Salnikov, Mikhail and others
entries.title: Adaptive Retrieval Without Self-Knowledge? Bringing Uncertainty Back Home
entries.claim: 35 adaptive-retrieval/uncertainty methods: many adaptive retrieval methods show near-zero self-knowledge; simple uncertainty estimators do as well.
entries.relevance: Retrieval/tool-request as a metacognitive control endpoint has been evaluated observationally -- not under competence lesions (as far as found).

entries.title: LLM-Independent Adaptive RAG: Let the Question Speak for Itself
entries.claim: Question-only features (27 features, no LLM access) match LLM-uncertainty methods for deciding when to retrieve.
entries.relevance: KEY EVIDENCE that on natural data, world/difficulty-tracking is observationally sufficient -- motivates interventional identification.

entries.title: SeaKR: Self-aware Knowledge Retrieval for Adaptive Retrieval Augmented Generation
entries.claim: Internal-state uncertainty triggers retrieval.
entries.relevance: Internal-signal-driven control precedent.

entries.title: Self-Monitoring Benefits from Structural Integration: Lessons from Metacognition in Continuous-Time Multi-Timescale Agents
entries.claim: Self-monitoring modules help only when integrated into the decision pathway (d=0.62, p=0.06, non-stationary); a parameter-matched control performed comparably.
entries.relevance: Closest prior to P5* integration claim; cautionary: apparent integration benefits can be architectural/parameter effects -> compute/param-matched nulls needed.

entries.title: Can Neural Networks Learn by Experimenting on Themselves? Self-Interventional Learning from Functional Consequences to Predictive Self-Knowledge
entries.claim: Networks perturb their own structure and learn a predictive self-model of functional consequences that generalises to unexecuted interventions; model-guided action not better than empirical memory.
entries.relevance: Closest prior to P5* 'self-variation' developmental regime; differs: no metacognitive monitoring of knowledge, no familiarity shortcut, no control under held-out lesions.

entries.authors: Nishi, Kento and Ramesh, Rahul and Okawa, Maya and Khona, Mikail and Tanaka, Hidenori and Lubana, Ekdeep Singh
entries.title: Representation Shattering in Transformers: A Synthetic Study with Knowledge Editing
entries.claim: Transformers trained from scratch on a synthetic knowledge graph; knowledge editing distorts representations of non-target entities ('shattering').
entries.relevance: Validated toy substrate for P5* and a known side-effect of edit-based lesions (must measure collateral damage).

entries.authors: Zucchet, Nicolas and Bornschein, Jorg and Chan, Stephanie C. Y. and Lampinen, Andrew Kyle and Pascanu, Razvan and De, Soham
entries.title: How do language models learn facts? Dynamics, curricula and hallucinations
entries.claim: Synthetic biographies: knowledge acquired after a plateau tied to recall-circuit formation; hallucinations emerge with knowledge; fine-tuning new facts corrupts existing memories.
entries.relevance: Synthetic-fact methodology + interference effects used as a held-out self-change (T3) in P5*.

entries.title: Physics of Language Models: Part 3.1, Knowledge Storage and Extraction
entries.claim: Controlled synthetic biographies show knowledge extractability depends on data augmentation diversity.
entries.relevance: Synthetic knowledge methodology for P5*.

entries.title: Recognition-Refusal Misalignment in LLMs: Why Models Answer Structurally Unanswerable Questions
entries.claim: Models linearly encode 'no admissible answer' but this direction is nearly orthogonal to refusal; steering it changes abstention (1.7B-70B).
entries.relevance: Monitoring signal exists but is not routed to control -- 'routing not encoding' failure analogous to anosognosia/anosodiaphoria.

entries.authors: Andrade, Katia and Guiyesse, Thomas and Medani, Takfarinas and Koechlin, Etienne and Pantazis, Dimitrios and Dubois, Bruno

entries.title: Rhesus monkeys know when they remember
entries.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
entries.claim: Monkeys decline memory tests more when memory is weak; no-sample probe trials (memory absent, cues/delay matched) show responding tracks the monitored memory state rather than the retention interval.
entries.relevance: D1: the classic input-fixed manipulation of the subject's own memory state to separate self-monitoring from cue-based responding; direct conceptual ancestor of N1's input-fixed competence change.

entries.title: Strangers to Themselves: What Language Models Say About Themselves Is Generic
entries.claim: Self-reports about own behaviour across nine evaluations are weak (r=+0.04); item-informed self-prediction (+0.24) is matched by a generic 'capable AI agents' framing (+0.28) and by other models' answers; net of the cross-model behaviour mean, self-report adds little (partial correlation +0.12); fine-tuning on own behaviour changes the behaviour being predicted.
entries.relevance: D1: a partial-correlation 'beyond shared knowledge' estimand (between-model, not pre/post); closest estimand relative found in LLM self-knowledge work.
entries.limitations: No input-fixed competence intervention; correlations across conditions, not within-target item-level change.

entries.authors: Kumaran, Dharshan and Daw, Nathaniel and Osindero, Simon and Veli{\v{c}}kovi{\'c}, Petar and Patraucean, Viorica
entries.title: Causal evidence that language models use confidence to drive behaviour
entries.claim: Activation steering of an internal confidence signal shifts abstention; models apply thresholds to internal confidence; verbal confidence independently predicts abstention.
entries.relevance: D1: causal test of confidence USE (steering the confidence representation), not of whether confidence tracks an input-fixed competence change.
entries.limitations: Intervenes on the confidence representation, not on competence.

entries.title: Me, Myself, and pi: Evaluating and Explaining LLM Introspection
entries.claim: Policy-introspection taxonomy; self vs other-model introspection accuracy as identification strategy; mechanistic 'attention diffusion' account.
entries.relevance: D1: self-vs-other cross-model identification logic (as in Binder et al.).
entries.limitations: No input-fixed competence intervention or within-target estimand.

entries.title: Continual Calibration: Coverage Can Collapse Before Accuracy in Lifelong LLM Fine-Tuning
entries.claim: Under sequential fine-tuning, conformal coverage and calibration degrade faster than accuracy (aggregate, per task); driven by score-distribution drift.
entries.relevance: D1/D2: confidence under self-generated capability change, but aggregate only; no item-level within-target tracking or pre-change adjustment.

entries.title: Looped Transformers under the Jacobian Lens: Does the Global Workspace Survive Recurrence?
entries.claim: Ouro-2.6B and Huginn-0125 vs Qwen3.6-27B: the workspace signature (verbalisable, causally steerable, selectively engaged) survives depth-recurrence; capacity 2.4/1.8/0.7 words; ignition width; Huginn persists content across recurrences, Ouro re-derives each loop. Loop count NOT manipulated.
entries.relevance: Closest neighbour for recurrence x workspace; leaves loop count as an IV and controlled training runs open.

entries.title: The Ignition Index: Measuring Global Workspace Dynamics in Language Models
entries.claim: Sigmoid steepness of layer-wise probe accuracy over a signal-strength sweep in 12 open models (GPT-2, Pythia, Gemma 2, Huginn, Mamba); iteration-axis ignition in Huginn; Pythia-410M changepoint at step 256. No causal test; no metacognition link.
entries.relevance: Probe-defined ignition only; causal ignition -> report remains open.

entries.title: The Cross-Substrate Access Assay: What an Indicator Test Must Declare to Travel from Brain to Language Model
entries.claim: Argues an indicator test must declare predictors, fitting, sampling unit, uncertainty target and decision rule; defines a cross-entropy estimand for two-state (ignition) vs graded access; EEG reproduction and simulation calibration (989 false two-state calls in 12,000 graded datasets); model-side protocol designed but not executed.
entries.relevance: Pre-empts part of D1 (declaration checklist) and makes a model-side ignition test time-sensitive.

entries.title: Evidence Integration in Large Language Models
entries.claim: Twelve LLMs; models accept invalid external candidates 93-100% despite internal verification; verification states decodable but little-to-no causal impact on answers; J-lens decomposition shows verification dissociable from integration.
entries.relevance: Monitoring-control dissociation with J-lens; neighbour of the control-routing candidate.
entries.limitations: Summarised from PDF via fetch tool.

entries.title: How LLMs Detect and Correct Their Own Errors: The Role of Internal Confidence Signals
entries.claim: Gemma 3 27B, Qwen 2.5 7B: a post-answer-newline (PANL) confidence representation is causally sufficient (patching restores ~74%) but not necessary (redundant with other positions) for error detection; predicts correction success.
entries.relevance: Causal error-monitoring neighbour; no workspace link; no factorial.

entries.title: Closing the Confidence-Faithfulness Gap in Large Language Models
entries.claim: Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Mistral-7B (base and instruct): calibration (accuracy) and verbalised-confidence directions are linear and nearly orthogonal; CAA steering shifts verbal confidence; joint solving inverts alignment.
entries.relevance: Confidence subspaces exist; no workspace link.

entries.title: Operational Proto-Introspection in Looped Language Models: Process-Quality Taps, Executable Branching, and the Readout-Control Boundary
entries.claim: Frozen Ouro-RLTT (2.6B, 4 loops): hidden states predict success beyond shortcuts, but no frozen intervention converts the readable signal into control ('the direction that predicts success is not a direction that, written back, produces success').
entries.relevance: Readout-control boundary; neighbour of the monitoring x control candidate.

entries.title: On Emergent Capabilities and Model Merging
entries.claim: LoRA merges of single-task parents cannot reach a superadditive capability of a jointly trained oracle (taboo extraction 23.7% vs <9.5%); the capability lies largely outside the parents' span.
entries.relevance: Closest precedent for 'integration produces superadditive capability' (not consciousness-related; weight merging only).

entries.title: The Pain Axis: LLMs Represent Self-Directed Harm and Act to Relieve It
entries.claim: Linear 'pain' direction across 25 open models, self-directed > other-directed; steering yields first-person distress; fine-tuned Qwen chooses a relief button even at a cost.
entries.relevance: Valence/self-model neighbour (category G).

entries.title: Language Models Can Control Their Own Attention
entries.claim: Prompted declarative protocol (<global>/<focus>/<local>) that masks KV attention; efficiency gains; no internal attention schema or AST link.
entries.relevance: Shows the implicit-attention-schema question is still open.

entries.title: Mechanisms of Introspective Awareness
entries.claim: Gemma3-27B, Qwen3-235B, OLMo-3.1-32B: injected-concept detection via a distributed anomaly-detection circuit (evidence carriers suppress a 'say No' gate); detection and identification use separate mechanisms.
entries.relevance: Injection-detection mechanisms; not metacognition about own knowledge.

entries.title: Reality Monitoring in Large Language Models: Self-Knowledge That Transforms with Conversation Memory
entries.claim: Source attribution (self- vs externally generated items) across six LLMs depends on memory structure; reading hallucination predicts failure.
entries.relevance: Source/reality-monitoring neighbour.

entries.title: ReCoN-Ipsundrum: An Inspectable Recurrent Persistence Loop Agent with Affect-Coupled Control and Mechanism-Linked Consciousness Indicator Assays
entries.claim: Toy agent; lesioning feedback/integration reduces post-stimulus persistence; affect coupling stabilises preference.
entries.relevance: Toy indicator-assay precedent.

entries.title: jacobian-lens: open-weight replication of the global workspace paper (OLMo-3 ladder, metacognition, ignition)
entries.claim: OLMo-3: post-training moves J-space ~31%; base workspace predicts own error AUROC 0.69 vs verbal 0.51; verbal self-evaluation rises with SFT; reviewer battery 2 clean / 1 partial / 3 inconclusive; introspection judged 'steering, not introspection'.
entries.relevance: Observational workspace-metacognition link (no causal ablation of metacognition).

entries.title: innerJ / JGateBench: benchmark and causal toolkit for J-space entry
entries.claim: Qwen3.6-27B: latent variables reach the verbalisable workspace by attention transport in a mid-depth window, not a gate; task demand increases visibility, not presence.
entries.relevance: Entry-mechanism neighbour of the causal-ignition candidate.

entries.authors: Butlin, Patrick and Long, Robert and Bayne, Tim and others
entries.title: Identifying indicators of consciousness in AI systems

entries.limitations: Author list partially from search result.

entries.title: The Global Workspace Needs Metacognition

entries.title: Predicting Where Steering Vectors Succeed
entries.claim: Linear Accessibility Profile (alignment with unembedding) predicts steering effectiveness (rho 0.86-0.91) and layer choice; Pythia-2.8B to Llama-8B, Gemma-2-2B, OLMo-2-1B.
entries.relevance: Output-aligned (verbalisable) directions steer better: a generic precedent for workspace-aligned writes; not about metacognitive control.

entries.claim: Directions that detect a concept can promote its opposite when used for steering (Gemma 3 12B, Qwen 2.5 14B, OLMo 3 7B).

entries.claim: Steering a verbal-uncertainty feature in line with internal (semantic) uncertainty reduces hallucination.

entries.claim: Qwen3-1.7B with a published J-lens: J-lens-inverted vectors steer all-caps well; refusal steering via J-space alone is weak.

entries.authors: Belrose, Nora and Schneider-Joseph, David and Ravfogel, Shauli and Cotterell, Ryan and Raff, Edward and Biderman, Stella
entries.title: LEACE: Perfect linear concept erasure in closed form
entries.claim: Closed-form eraser that 'provably prevents all linear classifiers from detecting a concept while changing the embedding as little as possible'; rank-1 for a binary concept.
entries.relevance: C15-R necessity operator: rank-1 LEACE restricted to the workspace subspace S_J (erase verdict access in J, keep F decodable in the complement).
entries.limitations: Linear guarantee only; nonlinear decodability can survive.

entries.title: The Hidden Signal of Verifier Strictness: Controlling and Improving Step-Wise Verification via Selective Latent Steering
entries.claim: Steering a latent correctness signal near verification-paragraph boundaries changes a generative verifier's accept/reject verdicts (sample-level 'selective' routing of the intervention).
entries.relevance: Generic sufficiency at the level of verification REPORTS; not use/control of a candidate, not workspace-route-specific.

entries.title: jspace-4b: Pre-registered J-space ablation study on Qwen3-4B: causal but not selective
entries.claim: Qwen3-4B with the neuronpedia lens (~437 MB): ablating the top-10 J-lens directions per position costs 16 points on a two-step reasoning control vs 0 for norm-matched random (n=55, McNemar p=.012) but changes 34-42% of ordinary next-token predictions (~2x random); the preregistered stop-gate refused the main experiment.
entries.relevance: Whole-J ablation is causally real but non-selective at 4B: C15-R necessity must be rank-1/LEACE, and the workspace label needs an explicit selectivity gate (W5).

entries.title: Worse Than Random: J-Space Ablation Is Anti-Selective at Every Measured Qwen3 Scale (jspace-validity)
entries.claim: Selectivity index (J-ablation damage on WikiText / local norm-matched random damage): 1.7B 3.38, 4B 2.17, 14B 1.57, 32B 1.16 (>1 = anti-selective); 1.7B and 32B preregistered; 8B stopped at a lens prerequisite; frontier scale untested.
entries.relevance: Published evidence that no CPU-feasible Qwen3 passes a norm-matched selectivity criterion; motivates assay-driven model selection and the SI_iso vs SI_norm decision.

entries.title: Do Large Language Models Latently Perform Multi-Hop Reasoning?

entries.relevance: Literature basis for the C15-R2 W0b' readout position t1, and evidence that the final position is a poor site for intermediate readout.

entries.claim: A trained back-attention module lets a lower layer (layer 6) of a frozen LLM attend to higher-layer states of all positions, then re-runs the forward pass; TwoHop 11.5->47.8 (Llama3-8B), MultiArith 21.1->88.9; ~0.002% extra params.

entries.title: Minimal and Mechanistic Conditions for Behavioral Self-Awareness in LLMs
entries.claim: Behavioural self-awareness can be induced by a single rank-1 LoRA adapter, largely captured by one steering vector; domain-localised.

entries.claim: Narrow fine-tuning activates a pre-existing persona structure; projecting it out prevents broad misalignment.
entries.relevance: Evidence that the persona-latent (EM) candidate is crowded.

entries.authors: Birch, Jonathan and Ginsburg, Simona and Jablonka, Eva
entries.title: Unlimited Associative Learning and the origins of consciousness: a primer and some predictions
entries.claim: UAL (compound and novel stimuli, second-order and trace conditioning, rewritable values) proposed as a transition marker of minimal consciousness; engineered systems with UAL-like learning but no hallmarks are declared 'derivative'.

entries.title: Unlimited Associative Learning as a Null Hypothesis
entries.claim: Standard causal-reasoning tasks can be explained by a powerful form of associative learning (UAL); urges broader hypothesis spaces.

entries.title: Consciousness & the small network argument
entries.claim: Most theories of consciousness can be implemented by small networks, so they are either incomplete or imply small networks are conscious.
entries.relevance: Precedent for minimal-system reductio arguments (UAL candidate).

entries.title: A Caveat Regarding the Unfolding Argument: Implications of Plasticity for Computational Theories of Consciousness
entries.claim: Rapid (perception-timescale) plasticity breaks the functional equivalence between a recurrent network and its unfolded feedforward network.
entries.relevance: Eliminates the unfolding-plasticity candidate (UF).
